paragraph: [Angola's parliament unanimously passed a start-up law in March 2026, according to ITWeb Africa and the Minister of Industry and Commerce](<https://itweb.africa/article/angola-passes-landmark-start-up-law/lLn14MmQwnVMJ6Aa>). [The law defines a startup by a maximum annual revenue of $3.5 million, with no minimum](<https://itweb.africa/article/angola-passes-landmark-start-up-law/lLn14MmQwnVMJ6Aa>). [The Council of Ministers had approved the bill in November 2025 and sent it to the National Assembly as urgent](<https://pti.ao/startup-executivo-aprova-proposta-de-lei-com-incentivos-fiscais-alargados/>). In the last twelve months Parliament took the bill from that approval to passage in March 2026. No source found since October 2023 says startups are labelled or registered under the law. Operating would need startups labelled or registered under the act, or its tax or other measures applied to them.

[Decree No. 2023-095 of 22 March 2023 sets how the start-up label is granted](<https://sgg.gouv.bj/doc/decret-2023-095/>) to micro, small and medium firms. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed. In October 2026 La Marina reported that [article 147 of the tax code exempts labelled startups](<https://lamarina.bj/2026/10/14/benin-vers-un-avantage-fiscal-des-startups-decompte-a-partir-de-lobtention-du-label/>) for two years. [The first labelling session, held from 2 to 12 December 2024, labelled fifteen firms](<https://lamarina.bj/2026/10/14/benin-vers-un-avantage-fiscal-des-startups-decompte-a-partir-de-lobtention-du-label/>). [La Nation's account of the October 2025 launch of the FAEN fund](<https://lanation.bj/economie/accord-adpme-biic-un-fonds-pour-propulser-lentrepreneuriat-numerique-au-benin>) names no investment made. Mature would need a public fund set up under the label to have financed startups, with investments named or counted.

[Agence Ecofin reports that Burkina Faso's AFP-PME is preparing a startup law](<https://ecomnewsafrique.com/2025/08/04/burkina-faso-le-gouvernement-burkinabe-a-engage-un-processus-visant-a-elaborer-une-loi-specifique-dediee-a-la-creation-au-financement-et-a-la-croissance-des-start-up-locales/>). [Its draft texts were examined at a national validation workshop on 17-18 July 2025](<https://ecomnewsafrique.com/2025/08/04/burkina-faso-le-gouvernement-burkinabe-a-engage-un-processus-visant-a-elaborer-une-loi-specifique-dediee-a-la-creation-au-financement-et-a-la-croissance-des-start-up-locales/>). [Drafting workshops had been held from March 2025](<https://directinfoburkina.net/burkina-faso-un-atelier-national-de-validation-des-projets-de-textes-juridiques-pour-la-promotion-des-startups-en-cours/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the law has been adopted, or that startups are labelled under it. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

No stage is set. [In November 2022 Trade and Industry Minister Mmusi Kgafela told Parliament that a Start-Up Act was under development](<https://dailynews.gov.bw/news-detail/70471>). [By February 2025 the Botswana Digital and Innovation Hub had financed startup IoT Communications through the Botswana Innovation Fund](<https://dailynews.gov.bw/news-detail/84714>). [The founder put the financing at P1 million](<https://dailynews.gov.bw/news-detail/84714>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found since October 2023 says whether a startup law or strategy is prepared or adopted. Preparing would need a startup bill drafted or tabled, or a startup strategy being written or in consultation.

[In July 2024 Finance Minister Hervé Ndoba said the state is perfecting the legal and regulatory framework of the startup ecosystem](<https://oubanguimedias.com/2024/07/12/centrafrique-le-ministre-des-finances-herve-ndoba-appelle-au-soutien-a-la-startup-centrafricaine-ikoue/>). [He announced a guarantee fund for startups and SMEs, coming soon](<https://oubanguimedias.com/2024/07/12/centrafrique-le-ministre-des-finances-herve-ndoba-appelle-au-soutien-a-la-startup-centrafricaine-ikoue/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a startup law or strategy has been adopted, or that startups are labelled under one. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

[Cote d'Ivoire adopted a Startup Act in November 2023](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/tech/cote-d-ivoire-calls-for-178m-fund-to-boost-tech-startups>): [law 2023-901 of 23 November 2023 promoting digital startups](<https://www.telecom.gouv.ci/new/uploads/publications/173214119048.pdf>). [It created a Digital Startup label with fiscal and customs incentives](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/tech/cote-d-ivoire-calls-for-178m-fund-to-boost-tech-startups>). In the last twelve months, [on 4 November 2026 the government named 14 start-ups and 18 small firms for 24 months of state support under the Act](<https://www.aip.ci/cote-divoire-aip-le-ministre-djibril-ouattara-annonce-24-mois-daccompagnement-de-letat-pour-32-entreprises-du-secteur-du-numerique/>). No source found since October 2023 says a public fund under the Act has financed startups. Mature would need a public fund set up under the act to have financed startups, with investments named or counted.

[In March 2025 the Nkafu Policy Institute said a Startup Act is proposed but not yet adopted](<https://nkafu.org/unlocking-the-potential-of-cameroons-startup-ecosystem/>). [Its November 2023 brief said a startup law had been in preparation at the telecommunications ministry since July 2021](<https://nkafu.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/SBEC-Report-english-Oct-2023-final-1.pdf>). [Dayspring Law Firm says the General Tax Code exempts eligible innovative ICT start-ups from tax for five years](<https://dayspringlaw.com/tax-incentives-for-innovative-startups-in-the-digital-industry/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a startup law or strategy has been adopted. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

[The DRC's Startup Act is ordonnance-loi 22/030 of 8 September 2022](<https://actualite.cd/index.php/2026/08/02/fiscalite-des-startups-congolaises-le-ministere-des-finances-met-fin-aux-mauvaises>). [Article 384 of the Digital Code makes digital start-ups eligible for its advantages](<https://www.wearetech.africa/fr/fils/actualites/tech/la-rdc-confirme-les-nouvelles-taxes-numeriques-mais-exonere-les-start-up>). [In May 2025 Cabinet adopted four draft decrees to apply them](<https://bankable.africa/fr/climat-des-affaires/2905-1244-entrepreneuriat-des-decrets-pour-activer-le-soutien-aux-startups-en-rdc>). In the last twelve months, [decree 26/022 of 5 June 2026 created a national labelling committee](<https://doseco.cd/2026/11/07/loi-sur-les-startup-4-ans-apres-la-promulgation-la-rdc-attend-toujours-un-dispositif-de-labellisation-operationnel/>). [It first met on 4 November 2026, with no secretariat or budget and no startup yet labelled](<https://doseco.cd/2026/11/07/loi-sur-les-startup-4-ans-apres-la-promulgation-la-rdc-attend-toujours-un-dispositif-de-labellisation-operationnel/>). Operating would need startups labelled or registered under the act, or its tax or other measures applied to them.

[On 2 July 2025 the Council of Ministers adopted decrees under law no. 71-2022 of 16 August 2022 on the startup label](<https://sgg.cg/ccm/compte-rendu-cmd-2025-07-02.pdf>). [They cover the label's withdrawal procedure and its labelling commission](<https://sgg.cg/ccm/compte-rendu-cmd-2025-07-02.pdf>). [In January 2024 the digital minister said young innovators with good projects pay no tax for five years under the law](<https://www.aci.cg/congo-numerique-caria-tech-village-un-incubateur-pour-assurer-lemployabilite-des-jeunes/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says startups are labelled or registered under the law. Operating would need startups labelled or registered under the act, or its tax or other measures applied to them.

[In May 2025 Secretary of State Pedro Lopes said Cape Verde has a dedicated start-up law with tax benefits](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/public-management/cape-verde-ramps-up-digital-start-up-ecosystem-to-boost-economy>). In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed. [A 2026 finance ministry deck says Law 70/VIII/2014 gives startups financial incentives and institutional support](<https://www.mf.gov.cv/documents/20126/0/Incentivos+Fiscais+do+Or%C3%A7amento+do+Estado+2026+%C3%A0+Di%C3%A1spora+Cabo-verdiana.pdf/77cb6457-8ea4-6d65-a08b-48f436baf849?t=1772281368148>). No source found since October 2023 says startups are labelled or registered under the law. [Fundo Morabeza, a €24 million government fund co-financed by the AfDB, funded 1,774 small firms in 2025](<https://www.fundomorabeza.com/en>). It is not shown set up under the law. Operating would need startups labelled or registered under the act, or its tax or other measures applied to them.

[On 9 November 2025 the minister for the digital economy presented the Startup Act bill to the National Assembly](<https://techafricanews.com/2025/11/12/djibouti-advances-startup-act-to-boost-innovation-and-youth-employment/>). It provides a startup label, tax incentives, a proposed national fund of funds and a startup visa. In the last twelve months, [UNESCO's 2026 country profile listed the Startup Act among Djibouti's legal foundations](<https://www.unesco.org/ethics-ai/en/global-hub/djibouti-0>), and [La Nation did the same in September 2026](<https://www.lanation.dj/premier-forum-national-sur-lintelligence-artificielle-djibouti-devoile-sa-strategie-nationale-2026-2030/>). [A guide on entreprendre.dj says an innovative, high-growth firm can apply for the Startup label](<https://entreprendre.dj/portals/g2b/guide>). No source found since October 2023 says any startup holds the label. Operating would need startups labelled or registered under the act, or its tax or other measures applied to them.

[El Watan reports 2,339 'projet innovant' labels issued between 2022 and July 2026](<https://elwatan.dz/strategie-nationale-de-lintelligence-artificielle-kamel-baddari-fixe-la-feuille-de-route/>). [In February 2026 about 2,300 of the more than 7,800 startups on startup.dz were certified as official startups](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/public-management/algeria-waives-ipo-fees-for-startups-until-2028>). In the last twelve months, [executive decree 25-311 of 1 December 2025 added a Scale-up label to the Start-up label](<https://legal-doctrine.com/fr/edition/creation-du-label-scale-up-lalgerie-renforce-son-dispositif-de-labellisation-des-start-ups-22429708315cfd1b44431f0a1183819d>). [By March 2026 about 15% of more than 100,000 applications on start-up.dz had won the label](<https://ouest-tribune.dz/startups-plus-de-100-000-demandes-de-labellisation-enregistrees-sur-la-plateforme-start-up-dz/>). No source found since October 2023 says a public fund under the startup law has financed startups. Mature would need a public fund set up under the act or strategy to have financed startups, with investments named or counted.

[Egypt launched its Startup Charter on 7 February 2026](<https://moic.gov.eg/news/2823>), a five-year startup strategy. [It sets an official startup definition, a financing initiative targeting USD 1 billion and a policy observatory](<https://moic.gov.eg/news/2823>). [Firms apply to the SME agency MSMEDA for a Startup Classification Certificate, which grants the official startup label](<https://www.clydeco.com/en/insights/2026/02/egypt-launches-first-national-startup-charter>). In the last twelve months, [by May 2026 MSMEDA had classified 61 companies under the charter, an MP said](<https://www.elbalad.news/6972755>). No source found since October 2023 says a public fund under the charter has financed startups. Mature would need a public fund set up under the act or strategy to have financed startups, with investments named or counted.

[Africa Legal reports that Ethiopia's Parliament unanimously approved the Startup Proclamation in July 2025](<https://www.africa-legal.com/news/ethiopia-shifts-towards-innovation-driven-economy-with-passage-of-startup-proclamation/122380>). It still had to be published in the Federal Negarit Gazette. [The Reporter says the proclamation, ratified on 17 July 2025, gives designated startups five-year tax exemptions](<https://thereportermagazines.com/4121/>). In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: [in November 2026 Minister Tamru said eligible startups would get incentives and support under the ratified proclamation](<https://techreviewafrica.com/news/8212/x>). No source found since October 2023 says startups are labelled or registered under it. Operating would need startups labelled or registered under the act, or its tax or other measures applied to them.

[In May 2026 Minister Doumba announced that a Gabonese Start-up Act would soon be finalised](<https://legabonais.com/bilan-des-100-jours-internet-cybersecurite-administration-numerique-marc-alexandre-doumba-deroule-la-strategie-digitale/>). [It would offer young tech entrepreneurs tax advantages, financing facilities and co-working spaces](<https://legabonais.com/bilan-des-100-jours-internet-cybersecurite-administration-numerique-marc-alexandre-doumba-deroule-la-strategie-digitale/>). That statement is the only position found in the last twelve months, and no earlier one has been found. No source found since October 2023 says the act has been adopted, or that startups are labelled under a startup law. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

[In September 2025 the ministry took a draft Innovation and Startup Bill to nationwide validation workshops](<https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-digital/2909-49082-ghana-sets-nationwide-consultations-on-draft-innovation-start-up-bill>). [It covers tax relief, access to funding and a certified startup label](<https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-digital/2909-49082-ghana-sets-nationwide-consultations-on-draft-innovation-start-up-bill>). In the last twelve months, [in May 2026 the Labari Journal listed the bill among 15 ICT bills](<https://labarijournal.com/ghana-is-considering-passing-a-host-of-new-ict-related-laws-an-analyst-says-they-would-hamper-africa-digital-trade/>) to be laid before or being considered by Parliament. [In July 2026 the communication minister, Samuel Nartey George, described the law as forthcoming](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/07/07/ghana-and-undp-strengthen-partnership-on-digital-transformation-projects/>). No source found since October 2023 says it has been adopted. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

[On 8 April 2025 a ministry workshop pre-validated the draft Startup Act](<https://gas-gn.org/?p=514>). [The draft gives labelled startups tax relief and sets up a four-year support fund](<https://gas-gn.org/?p=514>). On 29 April 2025 the commerce ministry [held a review of the draft startup law](<https://www.mipme.gov.gn/seance-de-relecture-du-projet-de-loi-sur-les-startups/>). In the last twelve months, [in July 2026 Guinée Alliance Startup urged the authorities to pass the bill](<https://fr.linkedin.com/posts/guinee-alliance-startup_l%C3%A9cosyst%C3%A8me-startup-au-c%C5%93ur-de-la-future-activity-7478024722543349763-xQOy>). In August 2026 the head of the payments firm Lengo Pay [said Guinea has no Startup Act](<https://business360.media/startups-guinee-diagnostic-dg-lengo-pay/>). Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

No stage is set. The higher education ministry [launched the National Research and Innovation Fund on 10 March 2026](<https://thepoint.gm/africa/gambia/headlines/gambias-national-research-and-innovation-fund-commissioned>). Its [Skills, Innovation and Entrepreneurship Fund opened a startup grant window](<https://gambiaj.com/economy/business/sie-fund-opens-startup-grant-window-for-75-gambian-youth-entrepreneurs/>) for 75 startups a year in August 2026. Both date from the last twelve months, and neither fund has named an award. No startup law or strategy has been found since October 2023. Preparing would need a startup bill drafted or tabled, or a startup strategy being written or in consultation.

[In February 2026 IDENTIC and the Bioko Chamber of Commerce stressed the need for legislation specific to startups and digital entrepreneurship](<https://realequatorialguinea.com/tecnologia/identic-y-la-camara-de-comercio-analizan-como-fortalecer-el-emprendimiento-tecnologico-en-guinea-ecuatorial/>). [They agreed to take proposals to the Senate](<https://realequatorialguinea.com/tecnologia/identic-y-la-camara-de-comercio-analizan-como-fortalecer-el-emprendimiento-tecnologico-en-guinea-ecuatorial/>). That statement is the only position found in the last twelve months, and no earlier one has been found. No source found since October 2023 says a startup law or strategy is being prepared. Preparing would need a startup bill drafted or tabled, or a startup strategy being written or in consultation.

[The Startup Bill, 2022 was published in the Kenya Gazette in December 2022 for the Senate](<https://parliament.go.ke/sites/default/files/2023-02/The%20Startup%20Bill%2C%202022.pdf>). [In January 2025 the National Assembly passed it](<https://nairobibusinessmonthly.com/mps-pass-startup-bill-to-support-innovation/>). [The Senate rejected the Assembly's amendments on 23 July 2025](<https://newsroom.hackhouse.africa/role-of-government-africas-startup-ecosystem>). In the last twelve months, [in May 2026 the bill was with a mediation committee and was not law](<https://newsroom.hackhouse.africa/role-of-government-africas-startup-ecosystem>). No source found since October 2023 says startups are labelled or registered under a startup law. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

[Libya's Prime Minister's Decision 23 of 2025 defines a start-up in law and took effect on issue](<https://lawsociety.ly/legislation/%D9%82%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%B1%D9%82%D9%85-23-%D9%84%D8%B3%D9%86%D8%A9-2025-%D9%85-%D8%A8%D8%A5%D9%86%D8%B4%D8%A7%D8%A1-%D8%B5%D9%86%D8%AF%D9%88%D9%82-%D8%AF%D8%B9%D9%85-%D9%88%D8%B6%D9%85%D8%A7/>). [Decision 23 of 23 January 2025 creates the Sunduq Intilaqa fund](<https://lawsociety.ly/legislation/%D9%82%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%B1%D9%82%D9%85-23-%D9%84%D8%B3%D9%86%D8%A9-2025-%D9%85-%D8%A8%D8%A5%D9%86%D8%B4%D8%A7%D8%A1-%D8%B5%D9%86%D8%AF%D9%88%D9%82-%D8%AF%D8%B9%D9%85-%D9%88%D8%B6%D9%85%D8%A7/>). [The fund gives startups seed finance and loan guarantees](<https://lawsociety.ly/legislation/%D9%82%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%B1%D9%82%D9%85-23-%D9%84%D8%B3%D9%86%D8%A9-2025-%D9%85-%D8%A8%D8%A5%D9%86%D8%B4%D8%A7%D8%A1-%D8%B5%D9%86%D8%AF%D9%88%D9%82-%D8%AF%D8%B9%D9%85-%D9%88%D8%B6%D9%85%D8%A7/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says startups are labelled or registered under the decision, or that its fund has financed any. Operating would need startups labelled or registered under the act, or its tax or other measures applied to them.

[The digital development agency created its JEI label in 2019](<https://www.lavieeco.com/tech/add-silence-on-digitalise/>). [By April 2025 it had gone to more than 540 startups from 1,303 applications](<https://www.lavieeco.com/tech/add-silence-on-digitalise/>). In the last twelve months, [decree 2.26.576 of 3 August 2026 strengthened the rules of the Startup Catalytic Fund](<https://themoroccopost.com/morocco-targets-258-million-in-startup-financing-through-new-venture-capital-mechanism/>). [The digital ministry set it up and Tamwilcom manages it, with $36 million of public money over three years](<https://themoroccopost.com/morocco-targets-258-million-in-startup-financing-through-new-venture-capital-mechanism/>). No source found since October 2023 says a public startup fund has financed startups, with investments named or counted. Mature would need a public fund set up under the act or strategy to have financed startups, with investments named or counted.

[On 27 June 2024 Minister Alhamdou Ag Ilyene said the Startup Act's adoption was imminent](<https://semainedunumerique.gouv.ml/ceremonie-de-cloture/>). [In October 2019 the Council of Ministers had adopted a start-up bill](<https://malijet.com/conseil_des_ministres_du_mali/234029-compte-rendu-du-conseil-des-ministres-du-mercredi-09-octobre-201.html>), which [set the legal framework for labelling and developing start-ups](<https://malijet.com/conseil_des_ministres_du_mali/234029-compte-rendu-du-conseil-des-ministres-du-mercredi-09-octobre-201.html>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the act has been adopted. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

[The digital ministry's page lists Law No. 2024-002 P.R on technological and innovative startups, dated 2 January 2024](<https://mtnima.gov.mr/fr/loi-de-startup/>). [The Africa Capital Report says the law establishes a labelling regime](<https://theafricacapitalreport.com/mauritanias-fintech-startups-met-investors-did-capital-follow/>). [In November 2025 the digital ministry was speeding publication of the texts completing the start-up law](<https://fr.tawassoul.net/mauritanie-ue-reunion-pour-evaluer-le-niveau-de-cooperation-numerique-bilaterale/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says startups are labelled or registered under the law. Operating would need startups labelled or registered under the act, or its tax or other measures applied to them.

[TechCabal reported in March 2024 that a startup bill was being drafted in Malawi](<https://techcabal.com/2024/03/02/malawi-tech-ecosystem-feature/>). [The bill was expected to reach parliament by the end of 2024](<https://techcabal.com/2024/03/02/malawi-tech-ecosystem-feature/>). In the last twelve months, [Tech Trends Malawi said in May 2026 that the Digital Innovation and Entrepreneurship Bill, proposed in 2024, never became law](<https://techtrendsmalawi.substack.com/p/malawi-needs-a-startup-act-like-yesterday>). No source found since October 2023 says a startup law or strategy has been adopted. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

On 26 November 2024 Cabinet [approved the National Informal Economy, Start-ups and Entrepreneurship Development Policy (NIESED)](<https://neweralive.na/cabinet-briefs-cabinet-decisions-issued-at-the-21st-decision-making-meeting-on-26-november-2024/>). The same decision [told the trade ministry to finalise an Act to accompany the policy](<https://neweralive.na/cabinet-briefs-cabinet-decisions-issued-at-the-21st-decision-making-meeting-on-26-november-2024/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. In September 2025 Cabinet [authorised the ICT ministry to engage female founders as potential beneficiaries of a US$20 million venture capital fund](<https://itweb.africa/article/namibia-expedites-data-centre-smart-city-development/KWEBb7yLVARvmRjO>). No startup has been found labelled under the policy, and no investment by the fund has been found. Operating would need startups labelled or registered under the act, or its tax or other measures applied to them.

In July 2024 [NITDA set up a Startup Labelling Committee to implement the Nigeria Startup Act](<https://nitda.gov.ng/nitda-dg-inaugurates-startup-labelling-committee-for-implementation-of-nigeria-startup-act/8254/>). The Act was signed in October 2022, with NITDA as its secretariat. [It sets up a startup label, a Startup Portal and a Startup Investment Seed Fund](<https://nitda.gov.ng/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/NIGERIA-STARTUP-ACT-2022-Final-Publication.pdf>). [About 13,000 businesses had registered as startups under NITDA's criteria by March 2025](<https://www.semafor.com/article/03/14/2025/nigeria-readies-40m-startup-seed-fund-backed-by-japan>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the Act's seed fund has invested in startups. Mature would need a public fund set up under the act to have financed startups, with investments named or counted.

[In June 2025 The New Times reported that the startup act had not been enacted or tabled in Cabinet](<https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/26957/news/technology/how-far-are-we-from-having-a-startup-act>), about five years after Rwanda announced it. The ICT Chamber's chief executive said several drafts were still being validated. No change has been found in the last twelve months. [The Rwanda Innovation Fund had backed 12 technology companies by 2024](<https://www.ktpress.rw/2026/07/why-tech-is-rwandas-fastest-growing-source-of-new-jobs/>), KT Press reported. No fund set up under a startup law has been found, and no startup act or strategy adopted. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

[In January 2025 the government adopted the implementing decree for Startup Law No. 2020-01 of 6 January 2020](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/tech/senegals-startup-law-advances-into-implementation-phase>). [The decree and the Ecosysteme Startup platform were launched on 20 November 2025](<https://aps.sn/ecosysteme-startup-un-nouveau-dispositif-pour-accompagner-linnovation/>). In the last twelve months, [by 30 June 2026 over 400 startups had registered on the Startup Act platform](<https://novotech.blog/article/budget-2027-du-numerique-la-pleniere-de-vendredi-est-bloquee-et-65-milliards-de>). [None had been labelled](<https://novotech.blog/article/budget-2027-du-numerique-la-pleniere-de-vendredi-est-bloquee-et-65-milliards-de>), as [no steering committee had been installed to award the label](<https://novotech.blog/article/budget-2027-du-numerique-la-pleniere-de-vendredi-est-bloquee-et-65-milliards-de>). Operating would need startups labelled or registered under the act, or its tax or other measures applied to them.

[In March 2024 the ministry and Columbia Law School began drafting a startup bill for Parliament](<https://sierraloaded.sl/news/sierra-leone-columbia-law-school-develop-modern-tech-law/>). In the last twelve months, in September 2026 the communications ministry and the International Trade Centre [held a validation workshop on a startup ecosystem policy](<https://www.techreviewafrica.com/news/7489/sierra-leone-startup-ecosystem-stakeholders-convene-to-strengthen-support-for-entrepreneurs>). On 12 September 2026 the communications minister [said the Act is expected in the first quarter of 2027](<https://sierraloaded.sl/news/fatima-bio-launch-flot-financial-platform/>). No startup law or strategy adopted has been found since October 2023. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

[In April 2026 Ibrahim Isse Abdulle wrote that Somalia has no formal legal definition of a startup](<https://somalistream.com/somalias-road-to-a-startup-nation-building-a-national-innovation-ecosystem/>). [He proposed a National Startup Act](<https://somalistream.com/somalias-road-to-a-startup-nation-building-a-national-innovation-ecosystem/>). [In August 2021 the commerce ministry's director of SMEs said there was no government funding for startups](<https://ilab.simad.edu.so/blog/lobbying-legal-framework-for-startups-in-somalia>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No startup bill or strategy being prepared has been found since October 2023. Preparing would need a startup bill drafted or tabled, or a startup strategy being written or in consultation.

No stage is set. [Resolution No. 39/2024 approves the National Strategy for Entrepreneurship in Sao Tome and Principe, 2024-2030](<https://www.informea.org/en/content/legislation/resolution-no-392024-approving-national-strategy-entrepreneurship-sao-tome-and>). The strategy names no measure for startups. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No startup law or strategy has been found since October 2023. Absent would need a source from the past three years that says no startup law, strategy or public support for startups exists.

The commerce ministry's [National MSME Policy 2024-2029](<https://www.undp.org/sites/g/files/zskgke326/files/2025-02/eswatini_msme_national_policy_2024-2029.pdf>) provides for a start-up matching fund and a fellowship fund for entrepreneurs. It also commits to review the tax requirements for start-ups. The policy sets adoption by Cabinet as its last step. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The [E45 million MSME Revolving Fund](<https://parliament.gov.sz/publications/parliament_reports/docs/ANNUAL%20REPORT%20COMMERCE%202025.pdf>) lends to start-ups. No source found says Cabinet has adopted the policy. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

[UNCTAD's 2023 National Entrepreneurship Strategy for Seychelles found no stand-alone Entrepreneurship Policy or Act](<https://unctad.org/system/files/official-document/tcsdiaeinf2023d2_en.pdf>). [It proposes only to consider introducing a Start-Up Act that would define innovative start-ups](<https://unctad.org/system/files/official-document/tcsdiaeinf2023d2_en.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a startup law or strategy is being prepared. Preparing would need a startup bill drafted or tabled, or a startup strategy being written or in consultation.

[In September 2025 Finance Minister Tahir Hamid Nguilin announced reforms under way](<https://www.toumaiwebmedias.com/tchad-le-ministre-des-finances-echange-avec-les-jeunes-entrepreneurs/>). [They include a legal and regulatory framework adapted to startups](<https://www.toumaiwebmedias.com/tchad-le-ministre-des-finances-echange-avec-les-jeunes-entrepreneurs/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a startup law or strategy has been adopted, or that startups are labelled under one. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

[African Business reports that Togo's Council of Ministers approved startup legislation in 2023](<https://african.business/2026/03/innov-africa-deals/togos-quiet-rise-as-a-startup-contender>). [The legislation has yet to be ratified](<https://african.business/2026/03/innov-africa-deals/togos-quiet-rise-as-a-startup-contender>). [In October 2025 the minister, Cina Lawson, said the Togolese Startup Act was being adopted](<https://togo-today.com/grit-lome-fait-vibrer-la-tech-africaine/>). In the last twelve months, [in May 2026 the opposition deputy Brigitte Adjamagbo-Johnson wrote that the bill on the innovation ecosystem was about to be adopted](<https://togoactualite.com/projet-de-loi-sur-linnovation-au-togo-une-ambition-necessaire-mais-un-texte-qui-nest-pas-a-la-hauteur-des-enjeux/>). No source found since October 2023 says a startup law is adopted. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

[A July 2026 report on a programme with Japan's JICA called the Startup Act the legal framework for startups](<https://www.lapresse.tn/2026/07/28/la-tunisie-et-le-japon-sallient-pour-renforcer-les-ecosystemes-de-startups-en-afrique/>). [Agence Ecofin reports that about 1,400 firms held the Start-up label in 2026](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/0911-143235-tunisie-356-8-millions-pour-la-transformation-numerique-en-2027-face-a-des-defis-persistants>). In the last twelve months, [in July 2026 the CDC's director-general said ANAVA had financed 10 investment funds](<https://launchbaseafrica.com/2026/09/24/tunisia-startup-fund/>), and through them 70 Tunisian startups were financed. [In April 2026 the minister said several ministries were still working on the revised Startup Act 2.0 bill](<https://www.lapresse.tn/2026/04/17/que-change-le-futur-startup-act-2-0-pour-les-startups-tunisiennes/>). Nothing found says how much ANAVA's funds have invested in startups.

[In 2024 the ICT ministry began drafting Tanzania's first National Startup Policy](<https://tsa.co.tz/storage/documents/w9Fsk1RQDCUKtfNiUXxOGijbCajKBHeuB8SNKwxx.pdf>), the Tanzania Startup Association reports. [In March 2025 the government opened consultations and a baseline study](<https://www.thecitizen.co.tz/tanzania/news/national/government-kicks-off-consultations-for-tanzania-s-first-startup-policy-4966048>). In the last twelve months, [in February 2026 the ministry said the draft Start-ups Policy 2026 was finalised and submitted for government approval](<https://dailynews.co.tz/govt-accelerates-digital-revolution-in-100-days/>). [In October 2026 Tanzania still had no dedicated startup law or policy](<https://www.tanzaniainvest.com/industry/startup-policy-within-six-months>), and the Vice-President directed that one be finalised within six months. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

[In May 2024 a ninth draft of the National Startup Policy was presented](<https://www.ecosystem.build/inside-the-uganda-startup-policy-journey/>), and a private member's Startup Bill was introduced in Parliament. In the last twelve months, [in June 2026 Startup Uganda said the National Startup Act was under technical review at the trade ministry](<https://www.linkedin.com/posts/startupug_startupuganda-nationalstartupact-policyleadership-activity-7476260216469368832-9mER>). [In November 2026 the Daily Monitor reported that the trade ministry was finalising a startup policy for Cabinet](<https://www.monitor.co.ug/uganda/news/national/startup-policies-are-underway-but-what-about-funding-for-the-young-innovators--5654650>). No source found since October 2023 says a startup law or strategy has been adopted. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

No stage is set. [In July 2026 Business Day said South Africa had no enacted startup act, and that one was proposed](<https://www.businessday.co.za/economy/2026-07-06-south-african-startup-growth-trails-regional-peers/>). [In February 2025 the science department said its public Innovation Fund had supported 12 venture capital firms and around 96 technology investments and enterprises](<https://www.gov.za/news/media-statements/science-technology-and-innovation-innovation-fund-21-feb-2025>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a startup bill is drafted or tabled, or a startup strategy prepared or adopted. Preparing would need a startup bill drafted or tabled, or a startup strategy being written or in consultation.

[In July 2024 Minister Felix Mutati said the government was working on a Start Up Bill to create a Venture Capital Fund for start-ups](<https://www.mots.gov.zm/?p=3864>). [In October 2025 he said the government had finalised the Innovation and Inventors Bill](<https://www.zambiamonitor.com/techbytes-zambian-govt-finalises-innovation-and-inventors-bill-sets-up-venture-capital-fund/>). In the last twelve months, [a Smart Africa workshop in July 2026 assessed progress on the proposed Startup Bill](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/07/02/smart-africa-and-zambia-advance-digital-entrepreneurship-policy-through-stakeholder-workshop/>). [The ITU's 2026 digital innovation profile says the Ministry of Technology and Science is finalising a Start-up Bill after consultations](<https://www.itu.int/en/ITU-D/Innovation/Documents/Publications/DIP%20Zambia/D-INNO-PROFILE.ZAMBIA-2026-PDF-E.pdf>). No source found since October 2023 says a startup law is adopted. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

In September 2024 [Zimbabwe's Cabinet adopted the principles of the Science, Technology, Innovation Start-up and Knowledge-based Economy Promotion Bill](<https://openparly.com/bill-alert-science-technology-innovation-start-up-and-knowledge-based-economy-promotion-bill/>). The bill would give start-ups tax incentives, rebates and preferential procurement. No change has been found in the last twelve months. In October 2026 the telecoms regulator's director-general said [its Innovation Drive Programme has given milestone-based funding to more than 100 innovations](<https://www.heraldonline.co.zw/potraz-says-it-is-now-a-gateway-for-investors-not-a-gatekeeper/>). The programme is not tied to the start-up bill. No source found since October 2023 says the bill has been adopted. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.
